LESSON: NUMBER RECOGNITION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: THEME: MY FAMILY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning
Topic 2.2: Number Recognition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Number Recognition, part of THEME: MY FAMILY Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learning in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Which number can you see on the flashcard?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Observe and talk about numbers on number flash cards or number charts in purposive groups/pairs, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication.

2. Talk about numbers found on objects in the home environment.

3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to identify numbers on flash cards or charts.

4. Sing /hum/clap/tap and dance to songs related to numbers while holding number cards, model numbers. During dancing learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use appropriate assistive devices while those with mobility difficulties could use relevant assistive technology to perform the task.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Observe and talk about numbers on number flash cards or number charts in purposive groups/pairs, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication.
2. Talk about numbers found on objects in the home environment.
3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to identify numbers on flash cards or charts.
4. Sing /hum/clap/tap and dance to songs related to numbers while holding number cards, model numbers. During dancing learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use appropriate assistive devices while those with mobility difficulties could use relevant assistive technology to perform the task.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Number Recognition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: learners talk to and listen to each other while collaboratively playing number recognition

games.

Values:
Love: learners share materials and work together as they play number games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-esteem: learners self-esteem is enhanced as they sing and dance to songs related to number recognition.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate the names of number symbols to reading similar vocabulary in Language Activities.
